summary: Barend J. ter Haar is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher and Susan Naquin, later holding posts at Heidelberg, Leiden, and Hamburg universities.

Barend Jan Terwiel is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Utrecht and the Australian National University, he held posts at ANU, the University of Munich, the University of Hamburg, and Leiden University.

Barnabás Csongor was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at the Budapest University of Technology and Economics and Eötvös Loránd University, where he taught from circa 1950 to 1988, and also held a post at Princeton University.

Barry Kerzin is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, USC, and with Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He taught medicine at the University of Washington and held posts at the University of Hong Kong.

Barry Sautman is a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology. He earned degrees from UCLA, NYU, and Columbia University. He held an assistant professorship at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology from 1993 to 2008.
Bart Dessein specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Willemen and serves as an associate professor at Ghent University (attested 2014–2026).

Bart Gruzalski is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Maryland, College Park, in 1974 and served as a professor of philosophy at Northeastern University.

Barthold Georg Niebuhr was an ancient historian who studied at Kiel University. He held academic chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1810–1813) and the University of Bonn (circa 1823–1831).

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He served as professor of Greek at the University of Virginia and professor at Johns Hopkins University.

Bazar Baradiyn was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, where he later taught, and headed the Buryat Scientific Center and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Stanford University and served as an associate professor of Chinese language and literature at Washington University in St. Louis (circa 1989–2021).

Beatrice Lane Suzuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied under William James, Josiah Royce, George Santayana, and George Herbert Palmer at Radcliffe and Columbia, and became a professor at Otani University in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer was a scholar of Indology and medical anthropology who studied at Heidelberg University. She held academic teaching posts at Heidelberg, the University of Maryland, the University of Hamburg, and the European University Viadrina.

Bedřich Hrozný was a Czech scholar in linguistics and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding academic posts at the University of Vienna and Charles University.
Beihō Takashima was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University and later held a post there.

Bela Bhattacharya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts as Professor of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and as Professor at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. from Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein in 2001. He served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences.
Ben Joffe is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan.

Benedetta Lomi is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London and held posts at the University of Virginia and the University of Bristol.

Benimadhab Barua was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of London, and served as a lecturer and professor of Pali at the University of Calcutta.
